person: a best friend who moved away
shape: small things you did without thinking as a kid that take nerve now, each told as what you did, never as advice

slides.text: things that were easy at nine but take nerve today
knocking on a front door and waiting on the mat, without calling ahead to ask if you were free
sitting on the grass at three o'clock with two cold cans, doing nothing until the shadow reached the fence
walking right up to someone by the swings and asking if you could play, before you even knew their name
dropping your bike on the lawn and leaving the front door wide open while you ran inside for [[two ice lollies]]
dialling seven numbers on the hallway wall phone from memory and asking someone's mum if they could come out
saying [[i miss you]] on the pavement at eight o'clock, without worrying if it was too much
save this for a tuesday when you need to send a simple text to the friend who moved away

caption:
we used to share a park bench for three hours with nowhere else to be.
now it takes six texts back and forth just to pick a night.
reaching out to my best friend used to be as simple as breathing.
save this for a quiet evening when you need a small nudge to type out a short hello.
